Tribunal.

The award was passed on 21.05.2019 whereby Rs.10,98,000/- alongwith 7% simple interest from the date of institution of the petition (29.07.2015) till payment, were .
awarded to the claimants.
Liability to pay the compensation amount was imposed upon two co-owners of the bus in question alongwith its driver (original respondents No.1 to 3).
Aggrieved, one of the owners of the bus in question has assailed the award dated 21.05.2019.
The challenge to the award is barred by 116 days.
Hence, the instant application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act has been moved for condoning the delay.

2. The ground put forth for condoning the delay in assailing the award is that Sh. Kanshi Ram (original respondent No.2,) the co-owner of the bus in question, was taking care of the interest of the applicant-appellant before the learned Tribunal.
The copy of the award was applied on 25.05.2019 and the same was delivered on 10.06.2019.

However, Sh. Kanshi Ram purportedly informed their learned counsel that decision regarding filing of the appeal shall be taken by the other partner i.e. the present applicant- appellant, who was in Saudi Arabia at the relevant time.
The applicant-appellant reached India in the month of October 2019.

Somehow, he remained under the impression that liability to satisfy the impugned award had been fastened on .
the insurance company.
It was only when he contacted his lawyer at Dharamshala, he came to know about the liability having been fastened on the owners and driver of the bus to satisfy the awarded amount.
Because of his ignorance about the imposition of the liability upon the owners, the appeal could not be preferred by him earlier.
r The appeal having been instituted on 14.12.2019, in the process, became delayed and barred by 116 days.
3. The respondent-insurance company in its reply took up the objection that the ground taken by the applicant- appellant for condoning the delay was patently false.
The applicant-appellant has not produced any material on record to show that he was actually in Saudi Arabia at the relevant time.

4. Faced with the aforesaid objection taken by the respondent-insurance company, the applicant-appellant time and again sought adjournments to file supplementary affidavit for placing on record materials to prove his presence in Saudi Arabia at the relevant time.
However, no supplementary affidavit till date has been filed by the applicant-appellant despite grant of repeated opportunities.

5. With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the matter is taken up for disposal at this stage.

6. In terms of its award dated 21.05.2019, learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal held the claimants entitled to compensation of Rs.10,98,000/- alongwith 7% simple interest from the date of filing the petition till payment.
The liability to satisfy the awarded amount was fastened upon the two co- owners and the driver of the vehicle, namely, present appellant, respondent No.4 and respondent No.5, .

respectively, with further observation that being third party claim, the insurance company-respondent No.6 would first pay the awarded amount to the claimants and then recover it from the appellant and respondents No.4 & 5.
Aggrieved against the imposition of liability upon the co-owners and driver, one of the owners has come up in the instant appeal.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
The only contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that liability to pay the compensation amount could not have been fastened upon the owners of the bus.
The above contention remains unsubstantiated.
No illegality or irregularity could be demonstrated in the impugned award fastening the liability to pay the awarded sum upon the owners and driver.
The bus in question did not have a valid route permit on the date of accident.

The accident had occurred on 25.05.2009, resulting in death of Sh.
Tilak Raj.
The claimants were legal heirs of Sh. Tilak Raj.
The route permit of the bus in question was placed on record as RW-4/B.
It has not been disputed before me that such route permit was valid w.e.f. 30.04.2004 to 27.03.2009.
Thereafter the owners of the bus got the route permit .
The route permit and its validity period were proved by RW-2 Sunil Kumar from RTO office Chamba.

The record made it evident that the bus in question Mohinder Singh vs Prem Lata And Others on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76115381/
3 did not possess route permit on 25.05.2009, when the accident took place.

sentences.text:
In 2018 ACJ 1768 (Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co.
Ltd. and others, Hon'ble Apex Court held that use of a vehicle in a public place without permit is a fundamental statutory infraction.

entities.text:
2018 ACJ 1768 (Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co.
Ltd. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This situation cannot be equated with absence of licence or a fake licence or a licence for different kind of vehicle or for that matter violation of a condition of carrying more number of passengers.

Relevant paragraph of the judgment is as under: -
23.
In the case in hand, it is clearly demonstrable from the materials brought on record that the vehicle at the time of the accident did not have a permit.
The appellants had taken the stand that the vehicle was not involved in the accident.
That apart, they had not stated whether the vehicle had temporary permit or any other kind of permit.

The exceptions that have been carved out under Section 66 of the Act,
needless to emphasis, are to be pleaded and proved.

The exceptions cannot be taken aid of in the course of an argument to seek .
absolution from liability.
Use of a vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction.
We are disposed to think so in view of the series of exceptions carved out in Section 66.

The said situations cannot be equated with absence of licence or a fake licnece or a licence for different kind of vehicle, or, for that matter, violation of a condition of carrying more number of passengers.
Therefore, the principles laid down in Swaran Singh, 2004 ACJ 1 (SC) and Lakhmi Chand, 2016 ACJ 551 (SC), in that regard would not be applicable to the case at hand.
That apart, the insurer had taken the plea that the vehicle in question had no permit.
It doe s not require the wisdom of the 'Tripitaka', that the existence of a permit of any nature is a matter of documentary evidence.
nothing has been brought on record by the insurer to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle.
In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer.

Therefore, the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed that the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver.

The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated tin Swaran Singh (supra) and other cases pertaining to pay and .
recover principle."

In view of the admitted facts of the case and the aforesaid legal position, no fault can be found in the impugned award, imposing liability upon the owners and driver of the bus in question for satisfying the awarded amount.
The appeal, therefore, fails and is accordingly dismissed.

The pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
